signature.name: Historic Centre of Quito
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed colonial old town packed with churches, plazas and balconied streets, and the first thing any visitor should explore. Go early in the morning for quieter streets and better light; it is walkable from most central hotels and taxis are cheap.

signature.name: Middle of the World City
signature.detail: The monument marking the equator, where you can stand with a foot in each hemisphere, is Quito's most famous photo stop. It is north of the city, so allow half a day and take a taxi or tour bus; go on a clear morning for views.

signature.name: Church of the Society of Jesus
signature.detail: This Jesuit church is famous for its gold-leaf interior and is one of the most ornate sights in the old town. Dress respectfully and note that a small entry fee applies; visit early or late to avoid tour groups.

signature.name: Virgin of El Panecillo
signature.detail: A huge winged statue on a hill with panoramic views over Quito and the surrounding volcanoes. Go on a clear day and take a taxi up rather than walking, especially after dark.

signature.name: Basilica of the National Vow
signature.detail: A neo-Gothic basilica with towers you can climb for rooftop views over the old town. Wear comfortable shoes for the stairs and ladders; a small fee is charged to go up.

transport: Metro $0.35 a ride; taxis short trips $2-4
